# Project Charter

## Testing Standards

- Unit/component tests: Vitest + @vue/test-utils (`npm run test:unit`).
- End-to-end: Playwright against the dev/preview server (`npm run test:e2e`).
- Type safety: `vue-tsc --build` (`npm run type-check`), no `any`-shaped escape hatches beyond documented `TODO(migration)` casts.
- Lint: oxlint + eslint, both with `--fix` (`npm run lint`).

## Quality Gates

Before a mission is merged: `npm run type-check`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run test:unit` must all pass. `npm run build` must succeed. `npm run test:e2e` is required for changes touching routing, auth, or a full view.

## Performance Benchmarks

No formal performance budget yet. Vite already warns on chunks over 500kB after minification — don't make that warning worse without a reason.

## Branch Strategy

Currently a single-maintainer project with direct commits to `main` (no branch protection or PR review in place today). spec-kitty missions introduce the first lightweight process: work happens in a mission worktree, goes through `spec-kitty review`/`accept`, then `spec-kitty merge` — adopt this for new feature work instead of committing straight to `main`.
Deployment: GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`) builds on push to `main` and deploys to GitHub Pages. Requires `VITE_FIREBASE_*` repository secrets to be set; the app degrades gracefully (no auth/data) when they're absent.

## Policy Summary

- Intent: Migrate "La Tour des Sorciers" — a homebrew French tabletop RPG campaign manager — from its original single-file HTML prototype (`legacy-reference/index.html`) to a maintainable Vue 3 + Firebase app, feature by feature, without regressing what already works.
- Languages/Frameworks: Vue 3 (`<script setup lang="ts">`) + TypeScript + Vite + vue-router + Firebase (Auth + Firestore client SDK, `firebase-admin` for seed scripts). Pinia is installed but stores are hand-rolled singleton composables, not `defineStore` — see CLAUDE.md.
- Testing: see Testing Standards above.
- Quality Gates: see Quality Gates above.
- Review Policy: see Branch Strategy above (mission-based review via spec-kitty, no standing reviewer today).
- Performance Targets: see Performance Benchmarks above.
- Deployment Constraints: see Branch Strategy above (GitHub Pages, Firebase secrets optional-but-degraded).

## Project Directives

1. Respect risk boundaries: Do not relax quality/security standards without explicit maintainer approval.
2. Keep documentation synchronized with workflow and behavior changes: Update docs (CLAUDE.md, this charter) whenever conventions or workflow semantics change.
3. Follow existing conventions: new stores follow the `useCampaignStore.ts` singleton-composable pattern; new repositories follow the `if (!db) return …` graceful-fallback pattern with `{ id: doc.id, ...doc.data() }` mapping. Don't introduce a second pattern for the same concern.
4. Treat `legacy-reference/index.html` as a behavior spec, not a code source — read it to understand intended functionality, then implement it idiomatically against the current architecture.
5. Keep user-facing strings in French, consistent with the existing tone.
